message.content:
Let  
\[
S=\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{\cos n\theta}{2^n}.
\]
Using \(\cos n\theta=\Re(e^{in\theta})\), we have
\[
S=\Re\left(\sum_{n=0}^\infty \left(\frac{e^{i\theta}}{2}\right)^n\right).
\]
This is a geometric series:
\[
S=\Re\left(\frac{1}{1-\frac{e^{i\theta}}{2}}\right).
\]

Let \(c=\cos\theta=\frac15\). Then
\[
1-\frac{e^{i\theta}}{2}=1-\frac{c}{2}-i\frac{\sin\theta}{2}
=\frac{9}{10}-i\frac{\sin\theta}{2}.
\]
The real part of the reciprocal is
\[
S=\frac{\frac{9}{10}}{\left(\frac{9}{10}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sin\theta}{2}\right)^2}.
\]
Now
\[
\sin^2\theta=1-\cos^2\theta=1-\frac1{25}=\frac{24}{25},
\]
so
\[
\left(\frac{\sin\theta}{2}\right)^2=\frac{24}{100}=\frac6{25}.
\]
Thus
\[
S=\frac{\frac{9}{10}}{\frac{81}{100}+\frac{24}{100}}
=\frac{\frac{9}{10}}{\frac{105}{100}}
=\frac{\frac{9}{10}}{\frac{21}{20}}
=\frac67.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac67}\).
